Global Leave Policy (Version 1) > 6. Sick leave

Employees receive 10 working days of paid sick leave in each leave year. Sick leave is credited in full on 1 January, or on the joining date for employees who join during the year, pro-rated by month.

Employees must tell their line manager as early as possible on the first day of absence. A medical certificate is required for any absence of more than 2 consecutive working days. Unused sick leave cannot be carried forward and is not paid out.

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 7. Sick leave

Employees receive 12 working days of paid sick leave in each leave year. For the 2026 leave year, the two additional days were credited to every employee on 1 April 2026. Sick leave is otherwise credited in full on 1 January, or on the joining date for employees who join during the year, pro-rated by month.

Employees must tell their line manager as early as possible on the first day of absence. A medical certificate is required for any absence of more than 3 consecutive working days. Unused sick leave cannot be carried forward and is not paid out.

All leave must be recorded in the HR system. Leave is counted in working days; weekends and public holidays that fall within a period of leave are not deducted from the employee's balance. Leave is taken in whole days.

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 6. Carrying annual leave forward

Employees may carry forward up to 10 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year. Carried forward days must be used by 31 March of the new leave year; any carried forward days not used by that date are forfeited. Unused annual leave above the carry-forward limit is forfeited on 31 December.

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 5. Annual leave

Employees earn annual leave each month according to the Annual Leave Accrual Schedule. Annual leave is paid at the employee's normal rate of pay. Employees are encouraged to take

at least ten working days of annual leave in each leave year, including one continuous break of at least five working days.

Annual leave must be requested in the HR system and approved by the line manager before it is taken. Requests for five or more working days should be made at least two weeks in advance.

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 10. Other absences

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 4. Definitions

- Leave year: the calendar year, from 1 January to 31 December.

- Working day: a day from Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday in the employee's office.

- Line manager: the person the employee reports to in the HR system.

- Primary caregiver: the parent who has the main responsibility for caring for a child after birth or adoption.

- Secondary caregiver: a parent who is not the primary caregiver.

A primary caregiver may take up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave following the birth or adoption of a child. Parental leave should be requested at least eight weeks before it starts.

- Annual leave is credited on the last calendar day of each month.

- Length of service is measured from the joining date to the first day of the month being credited.

- Employees who join after the 15th day of a month start earning from the following month.

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 1. Purpose

This policy sets out the types of leave available to employees of Veltrix Systems, how much leave employees receive, and how leave is requested and recorded. It aims to give employees time to rest, recover and care for others, while allowing teams to plan their work.

- Leave year: the calendar year, from 1 January to 31 December.

- Working day: a day from Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday in the employee's office.

- Line manager: the person the employee reports to in the HR system.

- Primary caregiver: the parent who has the main responsibility for caring for a child after birth or adoption.

- Secondary caregiver: a parent who is not the primary caregiver.

Global Leave Policy (Version 2) > 2. Scope

This policy applies to all permanent employees of Veltrix Systems in every office. A primary caregiver may take up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave following the birth or adoption of a child. Following the employee survey in April 2026 and a pilot in selected teams, we are changing our hybrid work arrangements for the Bengaluru (India) and Austin (United States) offices.

With effect from 1 July 2026, employees in these two offices may work from home for up to 3 days per week. The remaining working days are spent in the office. This replaces the limit of 2 days per week in the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy for these offices only.
